task: Quantitative stationary-law comparison and uniqueness for interacting single-site resampling systems
overall_status: finite theorem reconstructed; established comparison mechanism; novelty unsupported

claims.exact_statement: For finite V, binary replacement dynamics with site rates lambda_i>0, suppose q_i and qtilde_i have a common influence matrix C with TV(q_i(.|eta),q_i(.|zeta)) and TV(qtilde_i(.|eta),qtilde_i(.|zeta)) each at most sum_j C_ij 1[eta_j!=zeta_j]. If both processes use the same rates, delta_i=sup_eta TV(q_i(.|eta),qtilde_i(.|eta)), and spectral radius rho(C)<1, then both have unique stationary laws mu,mutilde and there is a coupling with p_i=P(X_i!=Y_i) satisfying p <= (I-C)^(-1) delta. Therefore TV(mu_S,mutilde_S) <= sum_{i in S}[(I-C)^(-1)delta]_i and |mu f-mutilde f| <= sum_i osc_i(f)[(I-C)^(-1)delta]_i.
assumptions: finite site set and finite spin space {0,1}
single-site replacement dynamics with positive site rates
a common, uniformly valid influence matrix for both kernels
same update rates in the compared systems
claims.novelty_boundary: The finite-volume result is a direct specialization of Dobrushin comparison / general invariant-Markov-kernel comparison. No novelty claim is made.
claims.falsifier: A discrepancy coupling violating the stationary coordinate inequality under the displayed common-clock and influence assumptions; none identified.

claims.exact_statement: For a countable-site finite-range Feller replacement process with rates uniformly bounded above and below, if positive weights bounded above and below satisfy Cw<=alpha w for alpha<1, common-clock coupling contracts the weighted sup discrepancy at rate at least lambda_min(1-alpha). The process has a unique invariant law. For a second process with the same clocks and common C, the stationary coupling obeys p<=sum_{n>=0} C^n delta.
assumptions: countable product of finite spin spaces
finite-range measurable replacement kernels and standard well-posed Feller graphical construction
uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on update rates
weights with 0<w_min<=w_i<=w_max<infinity and Cw<=alpha w, alpha<1
same clocks for the paired-process comparison
claims.novelty_boundary: Uniform Dobrushin coupling uniqueness is established machinery. The exact nonreversible generator presentation was not searched exhaustively and is not claimed as new.
claims.falsifier: A violation of local cylinder convergence or invariant-law uniqueness under the finite-range Feller and strict weighted contraction assumptions; none found.

claims.exact_statement: For a finite region Lambda and two frozen exterior boundaries b,bprime, if C_LambdaLambda bounds internal influences and C_LambdaB bounds boundary influences, then p_Lambda <= (I-C_LambdaLambda)^(-1) C_LambdaB 1[b!=bprime], and local-observable differences are bounded by summing coordinate disagreement times oscillations.
assumptions: boundary influences uniformly bounded by C_LambdaB
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical Dobrushin boundary comparison; no novelty claim.

claims.exact_statement: For q1(1|x2)=1/5+(3/5)x2 and q2(1|x1)=1/10+(1/5)x1, the local kernels are unchanged (delta=0) and rho(C)=sqrt(3/25)<1, but the stationary joint moment r is (lambda1*7/55+lambda2*39/440)/(lambda1+lambda2). Thus r=19/176 at rates (1,1) and r=151/1320 at (2,1); comparing only kernel perturbations is invalid when clocks differ.
claims.novelty_boundary: A scope counterexample, not a new phenomenon claim.
claims.falsifier: Directly recomputing the two stationarity equations for marginals and the x1*x2 equation; all displayed values are exact fractions.

claims.exact_statement: The weighted contraction condition is sufficient, not necessary. At low temperature the two-dimensional ferromagnetic Ising model has spontaneous magnetization and distinct plus/minus infinite-volume states, even though each finite-volume positive-rate heat-bath chain has a unique stationary law.
assumptions: infinite two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model at sufficiently low temperature
finite-volume comparison uses strictly positive heat-bath updates
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical low-temperature phase coexistence, included to delimit the contraction theorem.

prior_art.source: Patrick Rebeschini and Ramon van Handel, Comparison Theorems for Gibbs Measures, Journal of Statistical Physics 157 (2014), 234-281
prior_art.relevance: Theorem 2.4 gives a local-update Dobrushin comparison bound; Proposition 3.2 gives a general comparison principle for invariant measures of Markov kernels using Wasserstein influence matrices. A finite CTMC stationary law is invariant under its associated random-scan update kernel.

prior_art.source: R. L. Dobrushin, The problem of uniqueness of a Gibbsian random field and the problem of phase transitions, Functional Analysis and Its Applications 2 (1968), 302-312
prior_art.relevance: Classical uniqueness and phase-transition boundary for Gibbs random fields.

prior_art.source: Robert B. Griffiths, Peierls Proof of Spontaneous Magnetization in a Two-Dimensional Ising Ferromagnet, Physical Review 136 (1964), A437-A439
prior_art.relevance: Rigorous low-temperature spontaneous-magnetization result used to mark the phase-coexistence regime.

costs: Computing exact worst-case influence coefficients may require enumeration over all local boundaries; supplied analytic upper bounds are preferable.
The resolvent sums directed influence paths and can be expensive or loose if represented densely.
The comparison is conditional on certified C and delta values; they are not acquired for free.
limitations: The exact dynamics are single-site replacement/resampling processes; general spin-flip or jump IPS need a separate coupling drift bound.
Finite-volume uniqueness does not imply infinite-volume uniqueness or boundary independence.
The contraction condition is sufficient and failure of it proves neither coexistence nor slow mixing.
A different-rate comparison requires a rate-mismatch forcing term; the stated coarse term is conservative.
No code, simulation, external proof review, or exhaustive novelty search was performed.
open_questions: Can the nonreversible generator-level infinite-volume formulation be matched to an exact primary theorem beyond the general Markov-kernel comparison result?
Can rate-mismatch forcing be sharpened for noncompatible update kernels using the stationary coupling equations or a generator group inverse?
For a target finite-range nonreversible IPS, can one compute sparse C and delta bounds that yield a meaningful boundary response estimate?
